properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 3 at 2:48PM MST until November 3 at 5:15PM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...High water and flooding caused by excessive rainfall
continues.

* WHERE...Dolores River in western Montrose and Mesa Counties in
Colorado and eastern Grand County, Utah.

* WHEN...Until 515 PM MST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas. Some
low-water crossings may become impassable. River or stream flows
are elevated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 248 PM MST, High water levels have been observed due to recent
rainfall and runoff.
- Dolores River is the most likely place to experience minor
flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Gateway.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.areaDesc: Mesa, CO; Montrose, CO; Grand, UT

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 3 at 2:29PM MST until November 3 at 5:15PM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by recent rainfall continues.

* WHERE...South Central La Plata County in southwestern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 515 PM MST.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads
remain closed due to flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 229 PM MST, Flooding is already occurring in the warned area.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Animas River, Basin Creek and Lightner Creek.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Areas near Durango south to Bondad and the state line.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 3 at 8:11AM MST until November 4 at 6:46AM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Colorado...

Mancos River near Mancos affecting Montezuma County.

For the Mancos River...including Mancos...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Mancos River near Mancos and downstream.

* WHEN...Until Wednesday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 7.5 feet, residential flooding in Mancos is likely.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:00 AM MST Tuesday the stage was 7.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:00 AM MST Tuesday was 8.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage this
evening and continue falling to 4.4 feet late Saturday evening.
- Flood stage is 6.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 3:53PM MST until November 4 at 4:00PM MST by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
Flooding along the Conejos River and San Antonio River continues.

* WHAT...Flooding along the Conejos River and San Antonio River,
caused by recent runoff from upstream rain and snowmelt, is
occurring.

* WHERE...Eastern Conejos County in south central Colorado...
West Central Costilla County in south central Colorado...
South Central Alamosa County in southeastern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 400 PM MST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding along the Conejos River, from Mogote downstream
to Manassa, and the San Antonio River, near Ortiz downstream to
Manassa, is ongoing. Additional flooding of creeks, streams, and
other low-lying and flood-prone locations is possible. Numerous
roads remain closed due to flooding. Expect many areas of slow
moving or standing water through eastern Conejos County.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 347 PM MST, Upstream runoff from recent rain and snowmelt is
causing flooding into eastern Conejos County.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Manassa, Sanford, Antonito, Romeo, Alamosa East, Conejos and
Ortiz.
- http://www.water.noaa.gov
properties.areaDesc: Alamosa, CO; Conejos, CO; Costilla, CO

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 3:29PM MST until November 6 at 12:00AM MST by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Pueblo has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in Colorado...

Rio Grande At Alamosa affecting Alamosa County.

.Minor flooding along the Rio Grande through Alamosa is expected due
to upstream flooding occurring in the vicinity of Monte Vista.

For the Rio Grande...including Alamosa...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Alamosa.

* WHEN...From Wednesday afternoon to late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Minor flooding. Minor agricultural flooding
in low lying areas along the river.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:30 PM MST Monday the stage was 2.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage early
Wednesday afternoon to a crest of 9.6 feet late Wednesday
evening. It will then fall below flood stage early Thursday
afternoon.
- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.
- http://www.water.noaa.gov

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 12:31PM MST until November 5 at 5:15PM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding along the San Juan River caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...along the San Juan River from the Four Corners through
Mexican Hat, UT. This includes Bluff, Montezuma Creek and Aneth.

* WHEN...Until 515 PM MST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...River levels continue to rise due to excess runoff from
Sunday's rainfall. Expect high water levels and the River exceeding
its banks, inundating low-lying areas along the San Juan River. A
prolonged period of high water is forecast, with a crest near 23.5
ft Thursday morning. It will take several hours for all the water
from these storms to work through local drainage systems.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1222 PM MST, stream gauge reports upstream and impacts of
flooding have been reported along the San Juan River near
Farmington, NM. Expect flood waters to reach the Four Corners
Wednesday evening and the town of Bluff early Thursday morning.
Timing of crest is subject to change as more details become
available. Please continue to monitor the forecast and updated
warnings.
- At 11:30 AM MST Monday the stage was 20.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 22.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise to 22 feet late this evening with
a secondary crest near 23.5 feet expected near Bluff early
Thursday morning. It will then fall below flood stage Thursday
morning.
- Flood stage is 23.0 feet.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mexican Hat, Bluff, Montezuma Creek, and Aneth.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
